message.content: {"summary":"You developed a well-rationalised Australian reef-monitoring mission for CSIRO and BoM with solid STK access analysis. To elevate your work, resolve technical inconsistencies between your propulsion and manoeuvre plans, support orbital mechanics claims with verified hand calculations rather than relying on qualitative assumptions, and adopt rigorous academic presentation by replacing Wikipedia tables and citations with primary technical literature and standard captions.","next_steps":["Resolve propulsion contradictions by deciding between passive deorbit or active thrusters, backing your choice with drag-sail sizing and 25-year LEO disposal calculations.","Verify launch and orbit mechanics using hand calculations, correcting the misconception regarding equatorial launch assistance for retrograde Sun-Synchronous Orbits.","Replace all Wikipedia citations and raw tables with primary aerospace references, ensuring every table and figure includes consistent numbering and descriptive captions."],"criteria":{"C1":"You articulated a clear, compelling rationale in your Introduction, effectively establishing the need for Great Barrier Reef monitoring using fluid lensing. Your decision to deploy a single satellite was well-justified for CSIRO and BoM operational needs. To maintain top performance across future deliverables, ensure every cited operational constraint links directly to verifiable technical requirements.","C2":"You presented thorough STK access modelling in Mission Design. To reach Accomplished, eliminate contradictions—such as planning an EOL manoeuvre while stating you lack thrusters—and correct orbital claims regarding equatorial assistance for retrograde SSOs. Include explicit hand calculations, complete the truncated drag-sail description in Mission Duration & EOL, and quantitatively prove compliance with the 25-year deorbit guideline.","C3":"In the Conclusion, you effectively recapped the baseline architecture, including your launch vehicle and orbital regime. To reach Accomplished, draw detailed, evidence-based conclusions rather than generic summaries. Synthesise your quantitative STK outputs—such as ground access duration and revisit frequency—and critically reflect on mission feasibility and deorbit timeframes against design requirements.","C4":"Your report maintains a logical flow with an executive summary and table of contents. To reach Accomplished, replace unformatted Wikipedia tables and citations with primary aerospace literature. Ensure all figures and tables feature formal numbering and captions, clean up formatting in your Bibliography, and thoroughly proofread your text to prevent incomplete sentences."}}
